doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Settling in Chicago, the Sherman Hotel and the GI Bill at Roosevelt
summary: After discharge he works at the Sherman Hotel, hears the bands, and registers at Roosevelt under the GI Bill around early 1947.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So it seems like your target was Chicago after you were finally released from your service to your country.

I had a friend of mine I met there, when I met Jimmy Rainey. He said, “come to Chicago, and I’ll get you a job taking tickets at the Aragon.” It ended up that I got this guy a job hanging coats in the basement of the Sherman Hotel by the... what do you call that room... the Panther Room, where all the big bands played. And I was a runner for the girl photographer who used to take pictures of the conventioneers. I’d run the film down, they’d develop it, and I’d run it back up there and she’d sell it to the conventioneers.

Meanwhile I heard all the bands. Anyhow I also, of course they gave us the GI Bill, and I registered at Roosevelt, because that’s where most of the Afro-American, or I guess it was still black then, and Jewish people would go because they had a non-quota system. They were the only ones of a public college that had a non-quota system. I registered there and started taking courses.
It’s noted... Founded in 1945, so you started?
Around the end of ’46 or ’47. The beginning of ’47.
